choices: A function that takes no arguments and returns T
A function that takes T and returns a result
A function that takes T, performs some action, and returns nothing
A function that takes two arguments and returns a boolean
explanation: Consumer<T> has: void accept(T t). Examples: Consumer<String> print = System.out::println; list.forEach(print). BiConsumer<K,V> takes two arguments. Supplier<T> is the inverse: takes nothing and returns T.
